description: ABDUCTIVE EXPLANATION of a THIRD-PARTY actor's behaviour (never the conversation partner -- that is interlocutor_model's business, untouched here). domains/actor_goals.py's Python side is PURE ANNOTATION: for every actor-bearing predication `read_clause` grounds it writes ONE `ActorAction{actor, verb, object, object_domain, actor_role}` fact -- unconditionally, whether or not any codebook row will ever match it. `actor_role` is the RAW STRUCTURAL read (subject-position argument, or a passive by-phrase agent); `verb` is always reduced through `reading_collapse._participle_lemma` (held WordNet morphy) so active-inflected and passive-lemmatised surfaces key one codebook row. `ActionGoal{verb, goal}` (fund/sponsor/donate/back/finance -> 'support') is the teachable SURFACE-GOAL codebook; `RecipientVerb{verb}` (receive) is the teachable codebook for verbs whose grammatical subject conventionally names the RECEIVING participant rather than the causer (Levin's experiencer/goal-subject class); `ActorProfile{actor, core_interest, opposes}` is the teachable LAYERED-GOAL codebook (a handful, illustrative: oil_company -> fossil_fuels vs renewable_energy; cigarette_company -> smoking vs quit-smoking -- coal_company is deliberately NOT pre-seeded here, reserved as the TEACH-EXTENDS demonstration in the test suite). Three rules make every decision, in Rust: `mint_actor_goal` JOINS an ActorAction (actor_role=='agent') to an ActionGoal by Eq(verb) and mints a REVISABLE `ActorGoal{actor, verb, agency:'author', surface_goal, object, serves_conflicting_meta_goal:0.0, revisable:1.0}` (object is the action's own OBJECT DOMAIN, a mechanical premodifier-keeping token-drop -- see `actor_goals._object_domain`'s docstring -- never a fabricated goal value); `mint_actor_goal_recipient` JOINS the SAME ActorAction to a RecipientVerb by Eq(verb) and mints `ActorGoal{agency:'recipient', surface_goal:''}` instead -- the codebook JOIN is what tells the rule this verb's grammatical subject is semantically a recipient, never a Python `if verb=='received'`. `flag_conflicting_meta_goal` JOINS an author-agency ActorGoal to an ActorProfile by Eq(actor), gated on Eq(profile.opposes, goal.object) (the actor's declared core interest conflicts with THIS action's own object domain) and Eq(goal.serves_conflicting_meta_goal, 0.0) (fire once), and SETS `serves_conflicting_meta_goal:1.0` + the raw conflict fields (`meta_goal_core_interest`, `meta_goal_opposes`) + `mechanism:'undetermined'` on the EXISTING ActorGoal node -- DETECT, DO NOT FILL: no rule anywhere asserts a fabricated hidden-goal VALUE, only the conflict basis, and no rule anywhere asserts DELIBERATENESS. SEMANTICS (read before using this flag): `serves_conflicting_meta_goal` does NOT mean the surface action is fake, and it never attributes anything to the funded object or its recipients/beneficiaries (no rule below ever sets an attribute on anything but the FUNDER's own ActorGoal node) -- the project's governing principle is that many things are true at the same time: a funded renewable-energy project can be entirely genuine and good, AND its funder can simultaneously hold a higher-level goal that conflicts with the project's own domain. Both are true; this flag asserts only the second, about the actor's OWN goal layer. The flag is also MECHANISM-AGNOSTIC: a surface-vs-interest conflict is consistent with at least two distinct mechanisms this single act cannot discriminate -- (a) the actor knows a divergent goal and does not state it, or (b) an introspection gap (Nisbett-Wilson confabulation): the actor sincerely believes the stated reason, but it is not the actual driver, with no deliberateness or bad faith involved. `mechanism:'undetermined'` records this honestly on every flagged node; no rule ever picks (a) or (b). HONEST RESIDUAL: a single funding act only makes the conflicting meta-goal a DEFEASIBLE POSSIBILITY (revisable:1.0) -- the stronger evidence, a PATTERN across actions over time (fund the design, then lobby against its adoption) and named schemas for that cross-action pattern (Trojan Horse, Guilt-Based Action), is an explicit LATER SLICE, out of scope here. `held_actor_goals` (domains/actor_goals.py) is the mechanical reader.

microtheory.name: actor_goals
microtheory.description: an actor's action mints a candidate surface goal via a teachable verb->goal codebook, graded author/recipient by a teachable verb-class codebook, and flagged (never asserted) as possibly serving a conflicting higher-level goal when the actor's own declared interest conflicts with the action's object domain -- graph-joined judgments, revisable, never a Python if/else, and never a claim about the funded object's sincerity

attrs.note: funding something is canonically in service of supporting/promoting it.
sponsorship is canonically in service of supporting/promoting the sponsored thing.
donating is canonically in service of supporting the recipient/cause.
backing something is canonically in service of supporting/promoting it.
financing is canonically in service of supporting/enabling the financed thing.
'receive' is a goal-subject/experiencer verb -- the grammatical subject names the RECEIVING participant, not the causer (Levin's class), so its ActorGoal reads agency:'recipient', never 'author'.

illustrative: an oil company's declared core interest (fossil fuels) conflicts with a renewable-energy object domain -- the canonical layered-goal case; mechanism-agnostic (does not claim the funder consciously conceals anything, nor that the funded project is anything but genuine).
illustrative: a cigarette company's declared core interest (smoking) conflicts with a quit-smoking object domain.

effects.note: candidate surface goal, abducted from a teachable verb->goal codebook -- a genuine reading of what the action canonically serves
no authored goal -- the actor is grammatically the subject but semantically the RECIPIENT/beneficiary of this verb class, per the held RecipientVerb codebook, honestly no surface goal abducted
